findings.population: adults with sleep complaints (16 studies, 1,093 patients)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis (16 studies, 1,093 patients) concluded valerian might improve subjective sleep quality without notable side effects — yet 9 of the 16 studies had no positive sleep-quality outcome, doses ranged from 225 to 1,215 mg, and only one study used a standardized extract.
findings.limitations: the authors state the small, varied, often poor-quality studies mean the finding may not be reliable

findings.population: adults with anxiety disorders and subthreshold anxiety
findings.finding_summary: This updated meta-analysis of the oral lavender-oil preparation Silexan found it effective for treating anxiety across the included randomized trials.
findings.limitations: evidence is specific to the standardized oral Silexan capsule — it does not transfer to aromatherapy or unstandardized lavender products

findings.population: adults with generalized anxiety disorder (n=539, four-arm trial)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind four-arm trial, Silexan 160 mg/day reduced the Hamilton Anxiety total score by 14.1 points versus 11.3 with paroxetine 20 mg and 9.5 with placebo, with the 80 mg dose (12.8 points) also outperforming placebo.
findings.limitations: single manufacturer-supported trial of a proprietary preparation; paroxetine comparison was not powered as formal non-inferiority

findings.population: outpatients with mild-to-moderate generalized anxiety disorder (n=57 randomized)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, oral chamomile extract produced a significantly greater reduction in mean anxiety symptom scores than placebo over 8 weeks.
findings.limitations: small single trial in mild-to-moderate anxiety

findings.population: healthy young adults with mild sleep fluctuations (n=41, ages 18-35)
findings.finding_summary: In this double-blind placebo-controlled crossover investigation, one week of low-dose passionflower herbal tea produced significantly better subjective sleep-quality ratings than placebo.
findings.limitations: short-term tea-form study in healthy adults; direction of the endpoint is improved quality (insomnia-severity framing), not clinical insomnia treatment

findings.endpoint: sleep architecture (wake after sleep onset vs other components)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis found tryptophan supplementation shortened wake after sleep onset (about 81 minutes less per gram; supplementation at or above 1 g clearly better than below), while other sleep components — including sleep-onset latency — were unaffected.
findings.limitations: only 4 of 18 identified articles were meta-analyzable; the benefit is specific to sleep maintenance, not falling asleep

findings.finding_summary: This meta-analysis found beta-alanine supplementation significantly improved exercise capacity — with about a 2.85% improvement concentrated in efforts lasting 60 to 240 seconds — but did not improve performance-based outcome measures overall.
findings.limitations: benefit window is specific to 1-4-minute high-intensity efforts where muscle acidosis limits work; paresthesia at bolus doses is the familiar tolerability note

findings.endpoint: stress and sleep outcomes with oral GABA
findings.population: human clinical trials of oral GABA (14 studies)
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review of 14 human studies found mixed results: limited (low-to-moderate) evidence for stress reduction and very limited (low) evidence for sleep benefit from oral GABA, with the authors concluding more studies are needed before inferences can be made.
findings.limitations: oral GABA's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier remains contested, which is part of why the evidence base is graded so cautiously
